sherlock_holmes.name: Sherlock Holmes
sherlock_holmes.note: Consulting detective of 221B Baker Street, narrated through Watson's eyes; present throughout the cases in these divisions and the one who solves each.
sherlock_holmes.appearance_from_text: The text fixes little visual detail for Holmes beyond his being a sharp, cold, observant man and a convincing master of disguise; the look (lean, sharp-eyed, dressing-gown or ulster, pipe, violin) follows the brief and widely known Paget-style tradition.

stages.label: Sherlock Holmes
stages.text: Sherlock Holmes: man in his thirties; lean, wiry build; pale, angular face with a sharp, hawk-like nose and keen grey eyes; clean-shaven; dark hair worn short and neat. Dressed in a tweed suit or dark frock-coat, a long ulster or a dressing-gown in dark red or plum; pipe and violin as signature props.

quotes.quote: Accustomed as I was to my friend’s amazing powers in the use of disguises
Sherlock Holmes had been leaning back in his chair with his eyes closed
the measured tapping of Sherlock Holmes’ finger-tips upon the edge of the table

dr_watson.name: Dr. Watson
dr_watson.note: Narrator and Holmes's companion, a doctor; first-person voice throughout these divisions.
dr_watson.appearance_from_text: The text fixes almost nothing of Watson's looks beyond his being a married doctor who has put on weight since his marriage; the rest (age, build, dress, moustache) is supplied from the widely known Paget-style tradition of a sturdy, moustached Victorian army-surgeon type in frock-coat and tweeds.

stages.label: Watson, the narrator-companion
stages.text: Dr. Watson: man in his late thirties to forties, sturdy and solidly built with a comfortable, well-fed frame, having gained weight since marriage; fair to light-brown hair neatly parted, full drooping moustache, pleasant open face with kindly, steady eyes. Dresses as a respectable Victorian gentleman doctor in dark frock-coat or tweed suit, waistcoat, high collar and cravat; carries a physician's black bag and a walking stick, and often a revolver for dangerous nights.

quotes.quote: “Wedlock suits you,” he remarked. “I think, Watson, that you have put on seven and a half pounds since I saw you.”
I think, Watson, that it would be as well for you to have your pistol ready.

lestrade.name: Lestrade
lestrade.note: Ferret-like Scotland Yard detective; appears in the Boscombe and Noble Bachelor cases.
lestrade.appearance_from_text: The text fixes a lean, ferret-like, furtive and sly-looking build, a light brown dustcoat with leather leggings in the country, and a pea-jacket and cravat in town; the rest (age, hair, face detail) is supplied from the work's tradition and the era.

stages.label: Lestrade
stages.when: the Boscombe Valley and Noble Bachelor cases, across all seven sections
stages.text: Lestrade: a lean, wiry Scotland Yard inspector of about forty, with a ferret-like face, narrow sharp features and a sly, furtive cast to the eyes. Short, neatly brushed sandy-brown hair and a trim sandy moustache. Country dress: light brown dustcoat and leather leggings. Town dress: pea-jacket, cravat, and a black canvas bag in hand.

quotes.quote: A lean, ferret-like man, furtive and sly-looking
light brown dustcoat and leather-leggings
pea-jacket and cravat
a black canvas bag in his hand

221b_baker_street.name: 221B Baker Street
221b_baker_street.note: Holmes and Watson's shared sitting-room in London, the base for most of these cases.
221b_baker_street.appearance_from_text: The text fixes a first-floor sitting-room in Baker Street with a fireside, an armchair setting, a bow-window, a sideboard, a table with white cloth, gas lighting, shelves of old books and chemical apparatus, and a view onto a street of dun-coloured brick houses under fog and snow; the furnishing details beyond these are supplied by the Victorian tradition.

stages.label: Baker Street lodgings
stages.when: Across the stories, the shared sitting-room in Baker Street
stages.text: 221B Baker Street: first-floor sitting-room of a brick townhouse on a London street of dun-coloured brick houses; large bow-window onto the street; hearth with a coal fire and mantel; gaslit fittings; a sideboard and a table with white cloth; shelves of old books, chemical bottles and test-tubes; armchairs either side of the fire; violin and pipe on the mantelpiece; fog or snow outside.

quotes.quote: as we sat on either side of the fire in his lodgings at Baker Street
a cheery fire in the old room at Baker Street
Our gas was lit and shone on the white cloth and glimmer of china and metal
the snow of the day before still lay deep upon the ground
remained in our lodgings in Baker Street, buried among his old books
Down the centre of Baker Street it had been ploughed into a brown crumbly band by the traffic

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: Central figure of both the Gospel of Luke and the Gospel of John, son of Mary/Joseph of Nazareth, crucified and risen.
jesus.appearance_from_text: The text fixes almost no physical appearance for Jesus; it describes him as Nazareth-born, a Jewish teacher, and a man who is sometimes weary (John 4:6 style travel) and sometimes wept or groaned, so the look is supplied from the 1st-century Judean tradition and the owner's depiction rules (no halo, no stereotyped blue robe).

stages.label: Jesus of Nazareth, adult teacher
stages.when: Whole Gospel narrative, from the baptism and ministry through the crucifixion and resurrection
stages.text: Jesus: man in his early thirties; lean, sturdy build of a Galilean labourer; olive-brown skin weathered by sun and travel; short dark-brown hair and a trimmed dark beard in the manner of a 1st-century Jewish man; kind, direct, grave face with dark eyes; plain undyed linen or wool tunic in earth tones with a dark-blue or white fringed tassel at the hem of his cloak as a Jewish man would wear; a simple wool mantle; no halo, no stereotyped blue robe; no crown except where the scene is the mockery.

quotes.quote: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
The book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him.
Jesus therefore, again groaning in himself, came to the tomb.
The child was growing, and was becoming strong in spirit

simon_peter.name: Simon Peter
simon_peter.note: Fisherman apostle, brother of Andrew, called Cephas, who denies Jesus three times; the same disciple in Luke and John.
simon_peter.appearance_from_text: The text fixes almost nothing about his looks beyond his occupation as a fisherman with a boat and nets, his brotherhood with Andrew, and that he was naked while fishing and wrapped a coat around himself; the rest (age, build, dress, hair) is supplied from the first-century Galilean setting and the work's brief.

stages.label: Simon Peter, fisherman apostle
stages.when: Galilean ministry through the resurrection appearances
stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy Galilean fisherman in his thirties, weathered olive-brown skin, short dark curly hair and a full dark beard flecked with grey at the chin, broad calloused hands, a strong lined face. Wears a undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a rough wool cloak in earth brown or faded blue-grey, bare or sandalled feet; carries a fisherman's net or a folded coat.

quotes.quote: He entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s
he wrapped his coat around himself (for he was naked)
Then he came to Simon Peter.
Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it

moses.name: Moses
moses.note: Hebrew leader raised in Pharaoh's house, son of a Levite mother; flees to Midian, then leads Israel out of Egypt and receives the law at Sinai.
eras: Late Bronze Age Egypt and Sinai
moses.appearance_from_text: The text fixes Moses' age at eighty when he speaks to Pharaoh, his Levite parentage, his shepherd's work in Midian, his staff (rod), and his uncircumcised-lips speech difficulty and radiant face after Sinai; it gives no physical description, so build, face, and dress are supplied from the era and tradition.

stages.label: Moses, shepherd of Midian and prophet of the exodus
stages.when: Exodus 2 through 40, from the flight to Midian to the completion of the tabernacle
stages.text: Moses: man in his prime and then elder, aged 40 to 80 and beyond; lean, weathered build from desert shepherding; warm brown skin from sun; dark hair and a full dark beard, with some grey in later years; calm, grave face. Plain undyed woven wool robe with a simple linen belt, sandals; carries a shepherd's wooden staff, the rod of God. Dress is restrained and humble, never royal, though he was raised in Pharaoh's house.

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian
Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips
it became a rod in his hand.
he took the veil off, until he came out

david.name: David
david.note: Youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, anointed by Samuel, slays Goliath, flees Saul, becomes king.
eras: Late Bronze to early Iron Age Israel and Philistia
david.appearance_from_text: The text fixes that David is the youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, a shepherd who keeps sheep, is ruddy and fair-looking, carries a sling and stones, a sword and a shepherd's bag, is a skilled player of music, and that he later wears a robe and mantle as king. Build, hair, skin and beard are not described and were supplied from the work's traditional look for a Bronze-to-Iron Age Israelite youth.

stages.label: David as youth and shepherd
stages.when: 1 Samuel 16-18, youth before and at the victory over Goliath
stages.text: David: a youth of about fifteen to eighteen, slight but wiry, with a ruddy, fair complexion and bright eyes. Thick dark-brown hair cut to shoulder length, a short fine beard or none. Simple undyed linen or wool woven tunic belted with a leather sash, sandals; shepherd's leather bag slung at the hip and a sling of plaited cord, with a few smooth river stones.

quotes.quote: Fill your horn with oil, and go.
Your servant was keeping his father’s sheep
David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone
he had eight sons

stages.label: David as warrior and later king
stages.when: 1 Samuel 18-31, fugitive years and early kingship
stages.text: David: a man of about thirty, broad-shouldered and lean from years in the wilderness, with a ruddy, weathered complexion and a close-trimmed dark beard. Dark hair kept short. Woven wool tunic and mantle in deep undyed brown or earth-red, a leather belt with a bronze-hilted sword; a royal mantle of blue-purple trimmed with gold may mark kingship. Sling and shepherd's bag still at his side.

quotes.quote: Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him and gave it to David
But all Israel and Judah loved David
Behold the spear, O king!

goliath.name: Goliath
goliath.note: Philistine champion of Gath, slain by David with a sling.
eras: Late Bronze to early Iron Age Israel and Philistia
goliath.appearance_from_text: The text fixes his stature (six cubits and a span), his Philistine and Gath origin, his bronze helmet, coat of mail and greaves are not stated so these are supplied from the era's warrior dress, and his shield-bearer and sword are named; the brief's violence rule shapes the depiction of his death.

stages.label: Goliath of Gath
stages.when: the challenge and the duel, 1 Samuel 17
stages.text: Goliath: a giant warrior of about nine feet, towering and broad-shouldered, mature adult in his prime, bronze-skinned Philistine man of the Late Bronze to early Iron Age, close-cropped dark hair and a full beard, heavy brow and fierce set face, bronze helmet and scale-armour coat of mail with bronze greaves, a large round shield borne by an attendant, and a spear and sword at his side.

quotes.quote: whose height was six cubits and a span went out
the man who bore the shield went before him
You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin
The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth.

temple_in_jerusalem.name: Temple in Jerusalem
temple_in_jerusalem.note: The principal temple in Jerusalem where Zacharias serves, Jesus is presented and teaches, and Jesus cleanses the sellers; the Luke and John entries describe the same building and are joined.
temple_in_jerusalem.appearance_from_text: The text fixes that the temple is a large walled sanctuary with a veil, a treasury, colonnades called Solomon's porch, a pinnacle, an altar, courts where animals and money changers are found, and Mount Olivet nearby; its stone decoration is mentioned. Architecture, stone colour and exact layout were supplied from the Herodian temple tradition.

stages.label: Herodian temple, Jerusalem
stages.when: all scenes from Zacharias to the ascension, first century
stages.text: Temple in Jerusalem: a vast Herodian complex on a raised stone platform atop Mount Moriah, white and golden limestone walls with great dressed stone blocks, colonnaded porticoes including Solomon's porch, a gilded gate and a veil-screened inner sanctuary, courts thronged with pilgrims, oil lamps, altar of burnt offering, olive trees and the Mount of Olives rising beyond the eastern wall.

quotes.quote: how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts
the veil of the temple was torn in two
he would go out and spend the night on the mountain that is called Olivet
Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon's porch
his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense

ark_of_the_covenant.name: The ark of the covenant
ark_of_the_covenant.note: The gold-covered chest built in Exodus, carried into battle and captured by the Philistines in 1 Samuel.
ark_of_the_covenant.appearance_from_text: The text fixes the ark's material and dimensions (acacia wood, overlaid with gold per the wider Exodus account; about 2.5 by 1.5 cubits), its carrying poles through rings that are never removed, the mercy seat with cherubim on top, and the veil screening it; the gold overlay is stated in the tradition of Exodus 25 and the surfaces, finish and carrying gear are supplied by invention within the Sinai-era tabernacle style.

stages.label: Sinai tabernacle ark
stages.when: Exodus 25-40, construction and placement in the tabernacle
stages.text: ark of the covenant: a rectangular chest about two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide and high, of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold; a gold mercy seat lies on its lid with two cherubim facing each other above it; gold rings at its four corners hold two long carrying poles that are never removed; set behind a woven veil in the tabernacle's inner chamber.

quotes.quote: You shall put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry the ark.
The poles shall be in the rings of the ark. They shall not be taken from it.
from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the covenant
Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. Its length was two and a half cubits, and its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.
The veil shall separate the holy place from the most holy for you.

stages.label: Shiloh, battle and captivity
stages.when: 1 Samuel 4-7, carried into battle, captured, and returned
stages.text: ark of the covenant: a wooden chest of acacia overlaid with gold, with a gold lid and two cherubim, and gold carrying poles through its rings; the poles are carried on the shoulders of priests when it is moved, and it is kept under a veil or cloth when stored; no figure of God is shown, the box alone bears the presence of the holy.

quotes.quote: they brought from there the ark of the covenant of Yahweh of Armies, who sits above the cherubim
They carried the ark of the God of Israel there.
they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.
